items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: The interviewee reads an article about Clarence Waino's claims regarding Buddy Bolden and the origins of swing, but does not describe any personal interaction or relationship with Clarence Waino himself.

ctx.x: And this is what I'd like you to read. It was in 1918. If I got 1819 down there, it's the wrong date. I wasn't even in. It would have to be 1918 that we had these Mama's Baby Boy and Brown Skin, who you fought? I want you to read this here, part of an article. He says, Swing, as they call it today, by Clarence Waino. From Honky Tonk to Swing.

All right. Let's see. This is from Orchestra World, 1936. Let's see. All right. Swing, as they call it today, was originated in New Orleans, the birthplace of Sister Kate and many other standard swing tunes, such as Tiger Rag. In those days, you could find in the slums of New Orleans such places as the Red Onion, the Keystone, Pete Lawless, and the Odd Fellows Hall, where the Eagle Band used to play. The Eagle Band was one of the highest bands in the country, with Buddy Bolden Cornetis, who had the world beat…
